1.0.s.en: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

1.0.0.en: The former account that St. Luke the Evangelist wrote to Theophilus, whose name means "lover of God," is the Gospel of Luke. It contains the important works in the life of the Lord and all His teachings concerning the salvation of mankind. Note that Christ acts before He teaches, because words are easy, whereas the deed, which is the accomplishment of redemption, is the hard part. The former account was about the life of Christ on earth, whereas what he is about to write here is the work of Christ through the Apostles after His Ascension.

1.1.0.en: Here, in the Book of Acts, he will continue what the Lord resumed of His work and teaching after His ascension into heaven on the fortieth day after His holy Resurrection, and His commissioning of His disciples to preach the Gospel. Just as we must join words to deeds (v. 1), we must also make sure of the call of the Holy Spirit to us for service, through prayer and submission to the guidance of the Church.

1.1.1.en: Thus we see the continuity and connection between the Gospel, as the work of the Lord and His proclamation on earth, and the Book of Acts, as His work through His Apostles and disciples after His Ascension and by the Holy Spirit. Note that the Church reads the Synaxarium, which contains the saints of the day, after the Book of Acts, to declare that the word of the Lord grows, is strengthened and multiplies in His holy Church.

1.1.2.en: The position of the book between the Gospels and the Epistles links them together, because the Gospels are the life of Christ, the Book of Acts is the preaching of the Gospel, and the Epistles are how to live by it.

1.2.0.en: Christ proved His Resurrection by His appearances to His disciples and to those who believed in Him. He proved to them that He is alive by eating with them, by their touching Him and by speaking with them. He broke the bread in the same manner as at the Last Supper when He was with the two disciples of Emmaus, and He worked miracles such as the great catch of fish at the Sea of Tiberias. So the disciples were certain that He was their Teacher Jesus Christ, who had lived with them for more than three years on earth. He spoke to them about the things pertaining to the Kingdom of God in the hearts of His children in the Church, that is, He delivered to them the faith and the various rites of worship, because the disciples are responsible for leading the ministry in His Church.

1.3.0.en: While He was gathered with them, most likely toward the end of the forty days, He commanded them to return to Jerusalem and to stay there, because they had fled from it after the Crucifixion. He ordered them to wait for the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them, who is the promise of the Father, of whom the prophets prophesied, and of whom He had spoken to them many times during His life on earth.

1.4.0.en: Christ informed them that they would be baptized with the Holy Spirit, as John the Baptist had prophesied, after a short time, about ten days, when the Holy Spirit would descend upon them.

1.4.1.en: This is a clear indication that the disciples were baptized before the rest of the believers.

1.5.0.en: This is a gathering later than the one mentioned in (v. 4), for it took place on the very day of the Ascension. The disciples, like the rest of the Jews, thought that the kingdom of Christ was earthly; when He died their hopes were dashed, and then they were renewed by His Resurrection. When He promised them the descent of the Holy Spirit, they asked Him whether His kingdom on earth would be established on this day or later.

1.6.0.en: Christ did not answer their question or their mistaken belief about His earthly kingdom, leaving this until after the Holy Spirit had come upon them, so that by His power He would guide them to understand that Christ's kingdom is spiritual. He charged them not to ask about the times when God will accomplish His purposes, especially the Second Coming, because if they knew that it was far off they would grow careless, or if it was near they would be terrified. They need only prepare spiritually for the service of God.

1.7.0.en: Christ assured them that the descent of the Holy Spirit would be accompanied by great power in the spiritual life and in service. They continued to bear witness for eight years in Jerusalem until King Herod killed the Apostle James, and then they preached in Judea, which is the southern part of the kingdom of the Jews, and Samaria, which is the middle part south of Galilee. In the days of His ministry on earth, Christ had forbidden them to preach in it because of their weakness before the obstinacy of the Samaritans, being content with His own ministry in Judea. After that He commanded them to preach to the whole world.

1.7.1.en: Does the work of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in you through the Myron, appear in your words and deeds, whatever your circumstances?

1.7.2.en: Ask for God's help, whatever the adverse circumstances around you, and the Holy Spirit will support you.

1.8.s.en: (2) The Ascension and the return to the Upper Room

1.8.0.en: The Lord ascended in His body in the daytime before their eyes so that they would be sure of His ascension, and He disappeared in a cloud to confirm that He was lifted up into heaven and was not lost, to declare that His Kingdom is heavenly and that He went to prepare a place for us, so that we may lift up our hearts and prepare ourselves every day for heaven.

1.8.1.en: The cloud points to the presence of God, as happened when Moses received the commandments, and the cloud that covered the Tent of Meeting or Solomon's Temple when God came down and spoke with men, and as happened at the Transfiguration...

1.9.0.en: The eyes of the disciples remained fixed on heaven where Christ had entered in the midst of the cloud, their feelings either of sorrow at His departure, or of hope for His return shortly, or for some sign that would reveal His glory. While they were in this state, two angels suddenly appeared before them in the form of two men in bright white garments, to show the purity and majesty of heaven, and at the same time in the form of men so that the disciples would not be afraid of them. Their sudden appearance confirms that they were angels and not ordinary men.

1.10.0.en: The two angels spoke to the disciples in rebuke, because their eyes and hearts were still bound to Christ in the flesh, as He had lived among them on earth, and they were not yet able to live by faith and not by sight, although Christ had commanded them to stay in Jerusalem until the Holy Spirit came upon them, so that Christ would dwell in them and work more fully through the Holy Spirit.

1.10.1.en: They also informed them that Christ will come again on the Day of Judgment, so we must prepare for Him and live with Him, that we may rejoice on the last day.

1.11.0.en: The disciples returned to Jerusalem after the Ascension of Christ, which took place at the southeastern foot of the Mount of Olives, which is 2,000 paces from Jerusalem. This was the farthest distance the teachers of the Jews allowed a Jew to walk on the Sabbath, the day of rest, and they called it a Sabbath day's journey, because it is the distance between the farthest tent in the wilderness and the Tent of Meeting, so that they would permit walking it for a man to go to worship at the Tent of Meeting in ancient times.

1.12.0.en: The eleven continued in their prayers in the Upper Room in the house of the Apostle St. Mark, in spiritual unity. This is the fourth list of the names of the disciples, but Judas Iscariot is missing from it, who had hanged himself before this time.

1.12.1.en: There were with them women who followed Christ, whom the Gospels mention, such as Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, who was the sister of the Virgin, Salome the wife of Zebedee, Joanna the wife of Chuza, Susanna and others, all these in addition to the Virgin Mary, who had been living with John the Beloved since the Crucifixion of Christ. And His brethren: that is, the sons of His aunt, who believed in Him and became followers with the rest of the disciples. With one accord: for they were in fear of the Jews, in need of God's support, and longing to receive the power of the Holy Spirit whom Christ had promised them.

1.12.2.en: How pleasing it is to God that we pray in spiritual unity and with one accord in our homes and our churches, that the Lord may help His Church and His people.

1.12.3.en: So drive out of your heart all evil toward others, not only in the Divine Liturgy when you approach the Holy Mysteries, but also in your prayer in your inner room, that you may be of one accord with the rest of the believers, who are members of the Body of Christ.

1.12.4.en: Take care to feel for those around you and to pray for God's help for you all.

1.13.0.en: The number of believers in the house of St. Mark increased, whether from the seventy Apostles or those close to Christ, until it reached 120 persons. He called them disciples because all of them had become disciples and followed Christ during His life on earth. This does not mean that these were the only believers in Christ, but they were those close to Him, and so they include the eleven, the seventy Apostles, the Virgin Mary and the women who followed Christ, and perhaps Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus were with them.

1.13.1.en: They were praying in expectation of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them. During their gathering Peter stood up to speak, because he was by nature inclined to zeal and initiative, and he was encouraged in this by being the eldest of them.

1.14.0.en: Peter said to them: The prophecies have been fulfilled, as David said in (Ps 41:9) concerning the betrayal of Judas Iscariot and his handing Christ over to the Jews, for he guided them to His place in the Garden of Gethsemane and they seized Him and crucified Him. Judas was one of the twelve disciples, and was being prepared to be an apostle preaching Christ to the whole world.

1.15.0.en: Here St. Luke adds information that did not appear in Peter's address, because Luke is speaking to Greeks who do not know the events that took place in Jerusalem, so he explains them to them: that with the price for which Judas sold Christ the priests bought a field, so that he is considered the buyer.

1.15.1.en: The reward of iniquity: that is, the price of selling Christ, the innocent and wronged.

1.15.2.en: St. Luke also mentions how Judas Iscariot took his own life: he went to the mountain and tied himself to a high rock or a tree at the edge of the mountain, and when his body's weight hung on the rope he was strangled. Then the weight of the body increased, so that the rock broke away from the mountain or the tree broke, and he fell from a great height, and his body burst open and his bowels gushed out. It was a hideous death, a proof of the greatness of his sin.

1.15.3.en: The gushing out of his bowels signifies the exposure of his inner sins, which were in his heart while he followed Christ in a show that was different from the evil he concealed within.

1.15.4.en: This story was known to all the Jews of Jerusalem, and this confirms that the words are Luke's and not Peter's, for there was no need for Peter to mention it, since his hearers knew it, being all Jews of Jerusalem. Their proper tongue: that is, the Syriac or Aramaic language that was widespread among the Jews.

1.15.5.en: Aceldama, the field of blood: an indication that it was the price of the blood of Christ.

1.16.0.en: David says in (Ps 69:25) and (Ps 109:8) concerning the traitor Judas that his house will be laid waste, that is, his memory will be abolished, and another apostle will take his ministry.

1.16.1.en: In denunciation by the Church of the betrayal of Judas, these words ("Let his habitation be desolate") are read to a special melody, and a procession is made in the reverse direction to another melody, on the morning of Holy Thursday.

1.17.0.en: Peter saw the necessity of choosing a replacement for Judas from among those close to Christ, who had been disciples at His hands throughout the period of His ministry on earth.

1.17.1.en: Went in... and out: that is, Christ mingled with them and associated with them, and they were disciples at His hands.

1.17.2.en: The baptism of John: that is, from the time Christ was baptized by John and began His ministry until He ascended into heaven. That is, those who witnessed His ministry on earth.

1.17.3.en: A witness of His resurrection: the foundation of the preaching of Christ was the proclamation of the redemption accomplished on the Cross and revealed in the power of His Resurrection. So one of the marks of an apostle is that he has seen Christ and witnessed His Resurrection, and even the Apostle Paul, Christ Himself appeared to him to declare His Resurrection to him.

1.18.0.en: The disciples chose two persons, Justus and Matthias, whose name means "gift of God." These two persons were distinguished among the followers of Christ in their righteousness. It seems that they were so close that the disciples could not prefer one over the other.

1.19.0.en: The disciples prayed to God, who knows the secrets of hearts, to choose by Himself which of the two He wanted as an apostle in place of Judas Iscariot.

1.19.2.en: Ministry and apostleship: that is, the apostleship that Judas left, to be taken by the one chosen by God, so that the disciples would again be twelve, as Christ had chosen them.

1.19.3.en: To his own place: that is, the wicked Judas going to the place of the wicked, which is hell.

1.20.0.en: Then they cast lots, and God chose Matthias to preach in the name of Christ.

1.20.1.en: May we always seek God's counsel before undertaking any important work, through prayer and humility before Him, for He alone knows our interest and our good and searches the hearts of men, so that He protects us and guides us to what benefits us, and we trust in Him and accept His guidance even if it runs contrary to our aims.

1.20.2.en: The descent of the Holy Spirit and the birth and life of the first Church

2.0.s.en: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

2.0.0.en: The Feast of Pentecost was one of the three great feasts among the Jews, namely Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, at which all males were required to be present in Jerusalem at the Temple. It came fifty days after the second day of the Feast of Passover and was called the Feast of Weeks or of Harvest, in which every Jew offered the firstfruits of his harvest, and it fell on a Sunday.

2.0.1.en: The hundred and twenty gathered in the Upper Room continued in prayer until this day with one accord.

2.1.0.en: In the house of St. Mark there came a sound like the sound of the wind, but coming from above and not from the distant horizon as we are accustomed to hear the wind (compare Jn 3:8). This sound was to alert the people to what was happening in the Upper Room.

2.2.0.en: What looked like fire appeared, formed into divided tongues, flying in the air and then resting upon the head of each one of those gathered in the Upper Room, as a sign of the fiery tongues in preaching that God would grant them, because fire is a symbol of purification and power.

2.3.0.en: When the tongues rested on each one of them, all were filled by the working of the Holy Spirit, and to show this each one of them spoke in a language he did not know, according to the divine promise (Mk 16:17). Thus three miracles appeared, namely the sound of the wind, the tongues of fire and speaking in strange languages, to declare the descent of the Holy Spirit and the founding of the Church.

2.4.0.en: Jews from the various countries of the world came and dwelt in Jerusalem to attend the Feast of Pentecost. They were among the devout who cared for worship, as proved by their enduring the hardships and expense of travel.

2.5.0.en: This noise: that is, the sound of the wind, so the Jews gathered together, the news spread, and great crowds assembled around the house.

2.5.1.en: It seems that those who had gathered went out of the Upper Room into the crowds thronging there, and each of them spoke in a language foreign to the prevailing language among the Jews, which was Aramaic. Those who knew this new language gathered around him and were in great bewilderment: how could men who were weak in education and culture speak so many foreign languages well, especially since they were all from Galilee and had not gone to the other countries of the world with their foreign languages? The hearers knew these languages well as a result of having grown up in them from childhood, but it was strange that these Galileans should suddenly know them.

2.6.0.en: St. Luke shows the greatness of the miracle by the multitude of languages in which they spoke. He mentioned the various countries of the world from which the Jews had come, each one with its own language, and arranged the countries from eastern Asia to its west, then Europe, then Africa, and then returned to Asia again.

2.6.1.en: Parthians, Medes and Elamites: they dwell near Iran.

2.6.2.en: Mesopotamia: that is, between the Tigris and the Euphrates, which is Iraq.

2.6.3.en: Judea: the southern part of the kingdom of the Jews. They represent the largest number of those gathered, and their language differed to some extent in pronunciation from the language of the people of Galilee.

2.6.4.en: Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia: these are countries in the region of present-day Turkey.

2.6.5.en: Egypt: present-day Egypt, which at this time spoke the Coptic language.

2.6.6.en: Libya and Cyrene: present-day Libya, and Cyrene is a city in it, lying in North Africa, west of Egypt.

2.6.7.en: Strangers of Rome: that is, Jews who settled in Italy, and their language is Latin.

2.6.8.en: Jews and proselytes: that is, Jews living in countries other than Judea, or Gentiles who joined the Jewish religion and so were called proselytes. Whether the one or the other, they came from the countries of the world, each with his own language. Cretes: the inhabitants of the island of Crete.

2.6.9.en: Arabians: they live in the Arabian Peninsula.

2.6.10.en: The wonderful works of God: those upon whom the Holy Spirit had come were speaking about Christ, His redemption, His Resurrection, and His holy salvation for the whole world.

2.7.0.en: The hearers marveled at these languages and were bewildered in finding out the cause of this miracle: was it from God, or from some other cause?

2.8.0.en: Here the original Jews, who did not know these languages, began to mock, and thought that the Apostles and believers had drunk good wine, which is new wine.

2.8.1.en: Do not make light of the words of others or of any work they do, and do not hasten to judge it, but look for the good in it, and if you find a fault, find an excuse, so that your heart may be open to all and you win all, and at the same time keep your inner peace and your discernment of matters, far from tension and agitation.

2.9.s.en: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

2.9.0.en: Here we see Peter, whom the power of the Holy Spirit had changed from fear to courage, standing with the eleven to preach to the Jews who lived in Jerusalem and to the guest Jews who had come for the feast, and asking them to listen to him.

2.9.1.en: He spoke in the Aramaic language, which all the hearers knew because all were Jews, explaining that the disciples and believers were not drunk, because it is impossible for a Jew, however great his wickedness, to drink wine before the prayer of the third hour, which is the first prayer among the Jews (Isa 5:7).

2.10.0.en: Rather, this event is the fulfillment of the prophecy of Joel (Joel 2:28-32).

2.11.0.en: Servants and handmaidens: he means those lowest in rank in society, whether the poor, the uneducated or the enslaved.

2.11.1.en: The Holy Spirit comes upon all believers, whatever their social standing, and the proof of His coming is prophesying, not only in announcing the future, but more especially preaching and teaching, because he speaks of things to come, which is the Kingdom of Heaven.

2.12.0.en: Blood: that is, the killing of many, as happened in the persecutions in the ages of martyrdom.

2.12.1.en: Fire: huge conflagrations, as Nero burned Rome and accused the Christians of it.

2.12.2.en: Vapor and smoke: resulting from the fires.

2.12.3.en: The sun shall be turned into darkness: this is a strong sign that occurs before the Day of Judgment, when the sun loses its light completely.

2.12.4.en: The moon into blood: that is, its color becomes like blood, and this is something very terrifying that will also take place before the Day of Judgment. These signs have happened and are happening in part, and then will be completed before the last Day of Judgment, and they signify spiritual meanings, since heresies arise against the divinity of Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, to deny Him, and distort the image of the Church, which is the moon, with the smoke of heresies.

2.12.5.en: The work of the Holy Spirit is not limited to the beautiful promises mentioned in (vv. 17, 18), but also includes threats. Disturbances in nature, afflictions and persecutions occur to lead people to repentance, such as the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70. These disturbances are a prelude to greater disturbances that will take place before the last Day of Judgment.

2.13.0.en: God promised that whoever believes in Christ and repents of his sins will be saved, whether Jew or Gentile, that is, without distinction of race, and will escape all the preceding threats and receive the Kingdom of Heaven. It is clear that this verse is a comment on the preceding verses and cannot be separated from them, as claimed by the adherents of the heresy of universal salvation, who say that every person who calls upon the name of God is saved without faith in Christ or life in the Church. Thus they reject all the other verses of the Holy Bible that call for Baptism, Communion and all the spiritual practices of prayers and fasts...

2.14.0.en: God raised Him up: that is, the divinity united with His humanity. For Christ, in the form of weakness before the eyes of men, needed a power to raise Him, and that is the power of the divinity united with His humanity. Here he affirms that Christ is not separate from the God known to the Jews in the Old Testament, for it is He who raised Him because He and the Father are one, lest they fall into the heresy of two gods, one for the Old Testament and another for the New.

2.14.1.en: Peter explains to them that there are many proofs from the life of the Lord Christ showing that God worked miracles by His hand among them, and yet they seized Him and handed Him over to the Romans to kill Him.

2.14.2.en: In truth, that was the fulfillment of the counsel of God and His plan for the redemption of mankind by the death of Christ on the Cross.

2.14.3.en: Although it was the wicked hand of Pilate that issued the order for His crucifixion, they are the ones chiefly responsible for His crucifixion and death, because they demanded it and pressed Pilate to crucify Him. But God raised Him from the dead, and Christ triumphed over all the pangs that precede death, because He was stronger than death and it was impossible for death to subdue Him. This is the first time the Apostles preach the Resurrection, for Peter had changed from the weakness of denial, about fifty days before, to the courage of proclaiming and preaching by the power of the Holy Spirit.

2.15.0.en: On my right hand: it signifies strength and confidence in Christ, so that He does not fear death because He is able to rise.

2.15.1.en: Glad and rejoicing... in hope: this shows that joy did not leave Christ during His sufferings because of His hope of rising from the dead.

2.15.2.en: You will not leave my soul in Hades: that is, in hell, the place where the wicked wait.

2.15.3.en: Nor allow Your Holy One to see corruption: that is, it is not possible for Christ the Holy One that His body should suffer any change or corruption like the rest of those who sleep in the tombs.

2.15.4.en: The ways of life: that is, the way out of death into life by the Resurrection, relying on the power of His divinity united with His humanity.

2.15.5.en: You will make me full of joy: this is the joy at the resurrection of mankind through His Resurrection, and then His ascension into glory, so that men who believe in Him have the ability, through His redemption, to enter the heavenly glories.

2.15.6.en: St. Peter the Apostle cites the prophecy of David the prophet (Ps 16), which David the prophet did not mean about himself, but spoke in the person of Christ while He was in the tomb with His divinity united to His body, so that He is not troubled by death because the divinity helps the humanity, and He returns by the Resurrection to His glory and His joy at the accomplishment of salvation and the announcing of this to His children.

2.16.0.en: Let me freely speak: that is, it is permitted or possible or allowed.

2.16.1.en: The patriarch: because from his seed came all the fathers until Christ was born.

2.16.2.en: St. Peter affirms that it can easily be proved that David died and that his tomb is in Jerusalem.

2.17.0.en: According to the flesh: that is, with respect to the human nature of Christ, but at the same time He has the divine nature united with His humanity.

2.17.1.en: This confirms that what David said as a prophet is not about himself but about Christ, when he was taught by the hand of Nathan the prophet in (2 Sam 7:12, 16), and declared it in the Psalm (Ps 89:3, 35-37), that Christ would be born of his seed according to the flesh. And indeed the Lord came from the seed of David.

2.18.0.en: As David spoke in (Ps 16) of the Resurrection of Christ, and the triumph of His soul united with His divinity over Hades, and the preservation of His body united with His divinity from corruption until His soul returned to His body and He rose, as the Apostle Fathers testify.

2.19.0.en: Christ was glorified before all and ascended into heaven, and sent the Comforter Spirit whom He had promised His disciples, on this day in this miraculous manner which they see, in the form of tongues of fire, the sound of the wind and speaking in tongues.

2.20.0.en: All these words that David spoke do not apply to David himself either, but to Christ, for David did not ascend into heaven; rather it was he who conveyed by prophecy the conversation of the Father with the Son, which affirms the equality of the Son with the Father in essence and glory, because He said to Him, "Sit at My right hand," that is, after the accomplishment of redemption Christ returns to His glory in our sight, equal to the Father.

2.21.0.en: This is the accomplishment of the goal of redemption, which is the confining of Satan in the lake of fire and brimstone (1 Cor 15:24-28), and thereby the enemies of Christ, that is, Satan and death, are subjected under His feet forever.

2.22.0.en: All the hearers must know and believe that the Lord Christ is the Lord and Savior.

2.22.1.en: The Holy Spirit, who changed Peter from weakness to strength and to witness to Christ, is able to lift you from your weakness, whatever your sins, so that you may walk in purity.

2.22.2.en: Submit to Him by repentance, asking for His help, and partaking of the Holy Mysteries, and you will be strengthened in all your steps.

2.23.s.en: (3) The faith and Baptism of the multitudes

2.23.0.en: When they heard, they were deeply moved in the depths of their hearts and asked the Apostles for guidance as to what they should do, declaring their repentance and their readiness to carry out what the Spirit says on the tongues of the Apostles.

2.24.0.en: St. Peter answered, asking them to repent, to change their way, to declare their faith in Christ the Savior, one with His Father and the Holy Spirit, and to receive the sacrament of Baptism, so that their sins would be forgiven them and the Holy Spirit would come upon them.

2.24.1.en: Here we note the work of Baptism in the forgiveness of sins and the renewal of man's nature, for it is a condition for acceptance into Christianity.

2.25.0.en: Those who are afar off: that is, the Gentiles, for this is a proclamation that salvation is for the Jews and the Gentiles.

2.25.1.en: As many as the Lord our God shall call: by means of the preachers and servants.

2.25.2.en: The Apostle declared to them that the promise of eternal life is for everyone who repents, believes and is baptized, whether of the Jews or their children, who can also be baptized. For this reason the Church baptizes infants.

2.26.0.en: The Apostle continued at length in his sermon (not all of which is recorded in this book), bearing witness to the Lord and calling the hearers to accept Christ the Savior and to turn away from the crooked works of the wicked.

2.27.0.en: They received the word with joy and believed, repenting and being baptized. Thus the Church was born on the day of Pentecost, and the grain of wheat (that is, Christ), which died and rose, began to bring forth much fruit, which was three thousand souls.

2.27.1.en: When your heart is moved by the word of God, turn it into action through repentance and a serious way of life, with a self-giving love toward those around you, and submit to the fathers and guides, and you will know how to walk in righteousness and purity.

2.28.s.en: (4) The life of the first Church

2.28.0.en: Here we see the steadfastness of the new believers in the Lord, continuing in four basic things that distinguished the new community, which are:

2.28.1.en: 1- Listening to the teaching of the Apostles.

2.28.2.en: 2- Fellowship, that is, the love feast, which expresses unity.

2.28.3.en: 3- The breaking of bread, that is, Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord.

2.28.4.en: 4- Corporate liturgical prayers, that is, the Liturgy.

2.29.0.en: The fear of God came into the souls of the believers, which made them keep away from sins and walk in purity, and likewise the Jews and the pagans feared the Church as a community full of zeal and power. God supported them with miracles to confirm their faith and call many to believe in Christ.

2.30.0.en: The believers met together with one accord and love, which drove them not only to pray together but to consider what they owned as belonging to the Church, so that they distributed it to all, and what they had they could give to the Church at any time, because they were all members of the Body of Christ.

2.31.0.en: Many sold their possessions and divided the money among all according to their need, especially since many Jews who had come from the whole world to attend the Feast of Pentecost had settled in Jerusalem after accepting the faith, and they had no source of livelihood in the Jewish land.

2.32.0.en: Worship in the Temple was in Solomon's Porch beside the Beautiful Gate, the only ancient part of the Temple that was not demolished at the exile since Solomon built it. They kept the unity of the Spirit, and besides this they prayed and celebrated the sacrament of the Eucharist in the houses, rejoicing in the Lord in whom they had believed and who had given them simplicity of heart.

2.33.0.en: The believers were distinguished by praising and thanking God with joy, so the Jews loved them because of the purity of their conduct and their compassion for the poor. This helped the Holy Spirit bring many to faith every day.

2.33.1.en: Do you feel your union in the Church with the rest of the believers, so that you take care to attend the Liturgies and the spiritual meetings?

2.33.2.en: And do you seek to meet the needs of others and feel that all you own belongs to God and the Church? If you do this, then God will keep you in a pure life and give you favor in the eyes of those around you. The healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate
